primary_meaning: Sacred rest: the Sabbath is most commonly understood as symbolizing participation in God’s own rest, fulfilled spiritually in rest or salvation in Christ and ultimately in eternal or eschatological rest.
primary_basis: Genesis 2:2–3 — God rests on the seventh day and blesses it.
Exodus 20:8–11 — Sabbath rest is grounded in God’s creation rest.
Matthew 11:28–30 — Jesus offers rest to those who come to him.
Colossians 2:16–17 — Sabbaths are described as a shadow whose substance belongs to Christ.
Hebrews 3:7–4:11 — entry into God’s rest remains available, and a Sabbath-rest remains for God’s people.
Revelation 14:13 — the blessed dead rest from their labors.

alternatives.meaning: A continuing creation ordinance and recurring literal seventh-day holy rest, rather than chiefly a symbol displaced by its fulfillment.
A covenant sign specifically identifying and sanctifying Israel under the Mosaic covenant.
A memorial of deliverance from slavery and therefore a sign of liberation, humane treatment, and social justice.
A pattern transferred to the Christian Lord’s Day, with Sunday commemorating Christ’s resurrection and anticipating the final renewal.
A prophetic type of a future millennial ‘seventh age’ or thousand-year reign.

notes: There is broad Christian agreement that rest is the Sabbath’s central symbolic field. There is no fully settled consensus about the referent of that rest: traditions variously emphasize present rest in Christ, future heavenly rest, literal weekly observance, Israel’s covenant sign, liberation, or Sunday/Lord’s Day fulfillment.
